description: The gate and the train as services (GATE-TRAIN-SERVICES, D-086, ADR-41): the Tower runner, its transports and the status, health and metrics surface.

service.control_timeout_s.description: Timeout of one control-plane HTTP request. The job deadline further bounds runner calls; a failed request is reported without selecting another transport.

service.control_url.description: Base URL of the control plane (the Cloudflare Worker forge-webhook, retired with D-323: no implementation answers it today): /status, /healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /events, the runner and admin calls.

service.db_alert_connections_ratio.description: DB-VITALS (docs/operations/aws-revisao-arquitetura.md, finding 13): the share of the database's max_connections the peak of open connections may reach before the live service alerts (platform.db.vitals alerts: connections). The peak is the largest count of pg_stat_activity seen on the service's heartbeats in the event's window; past max_connections every new login fails and the engine stops at once.

service.db_alert_disk_ratio.description: DB-VITALS (docs/operations/aws-revisao-arquitetura.md, finding 10): the share of service.db_disk_bytes the database may take before the live service alerts (platform.db.vitals alerts: disk, published to the platform's topic once when it starts and once when it ends). The database's size leaves out the write-ahead log and the temporary files, so the alert comes with room left: 0.7 of 20 GiB leaves 6 GiB.

service.db_disk_bytes.description: DB-VITALS (docs/operations/aws-revisao-arquitetura.md, finding 10): the allocated disk of the engine's database, in bytes (the RDS instance has 20 GiB; Postgres cannot read it). The live service divides the database's size by it (platform.db.vitals disk_ratio) to say how full the disk is; a change of the instance's storage is followed by PUT /v1/config/service.db_disk_bytes.

service.dispatch_s.description: The dispatcher's safety tick (DEP9): the longest the infrastructure service waits between two passes when no notification wakes it (work freed, a run started). It is a failure timeout, not a trigger: the passes are woken by LISTEN/NOTIFY (migration 0006). Read at runtime from work.config_value, the compiled default when no row exists; PUT /v1/config/service.dispatch_s changes it within about a second, without a deploy.

service.dispatch_stall_alert_s.description: DISPATCH-STALL-ALERT (docs/operations/aws-revisao-arquitetura.md, finding 32): how long, in seconds, a job that a dispatcher would start now (a first candidate of its queue whose route has a free slot it may take) may stay queued before a service process that stands by alerts (platform.dispatch.stalled, published to the platform's topic once when it starts and once when it ends). A live dispatcher starts such a job on its next tick (service.dispatch_s, 1 s), and a service that takes the role over does it within seconds of the swap or of a failover (deploy.live_stale_s, 10 s); 120 s is past every one of those and well under the 7.7 minutes of 11/11 with no dispatch and no alert.

service.engine_repo.description: The engine's repository on its forge: the one the service's looks (canary, checks, observations, branches) read and judge. The service reads it live from the port (PUT /v1/config/service.engine_repo); TOWER_ENGINE_REPO in the service's environment wins over it. A value that is not owner/name is refused by the port and ignored by the reader.
service.engine_repo.x-source: Torre 14/11 (GitHub migration): the repository identity comes from configuration

service.gate_command.description: The real per-PR gate, with the PR number appended. It runs the actual stages and content-keyed test proofs under the enforced service.job_budget_s; absence of a whole-gate attestation never substitutes for running it (D-291).

service.heartbeat_stale_s.description: A runner whose heartbeat is older than this fails the runner health check.

service.job_budget_s.description: The budget of one runner job from its claim to its result (D-291; Daniel 02/11 23:06 BRT: 180 s; 23:35 BRT: 300 s, the measured tier 2 of 162 s plus margin, I-ddaca17c). The one source of the budget: the runner reads it from its checkout's registry (the control plane Worker that leased a claimed job for this long is retired, D-323). The runner hands the job its deadline (TOWER_JOB_DEADLINE), sends TERM one second before it and KILL at it, and answers over_budget with the phase that was running; the train's lock expires at the same deadline, so a dead holder never blocks the next job past it.

service.jobs_dir.description: Directory, relative to the runner's checkout, of each job's whole output (<job id>.log).

service.latency_quantiles.description: The quantiles `scripts/service metrics` reports for each latency (green to merged), by nearest rank: p50 and p95, the shape of the targets (intake T2, T3).

service.lock_stale_s.description: A train lock whose lease ended longer ago than this, and was never released, warns the lock health check (the lease frees it; the warning names a train that died).

service.log_max_bytes.description: Size past which the runner's JSONL log is rotated.

service.log_path.description: The runner's JSONL log, beside its state file: one line per queued, finished, cancelled or paused job and per failed poll, rotated to .1 past service.log_max_bytes.

service.log_tail_chars.description: The tail of a job's output carried in its result (contracts/service/result.v1.json log_tail, at most 4000).

service.paused.description: The pause switch of the gate and train services (D-086): while true a Tower runner claims no new job and the control plane dispatches none; a running job finishes. Flipped with `scripts/service pause|resume --reason` through the shared store (D-069 item 5), never a local override.

service.poll_s.description: Seconds between two polls of a Tower runner: one round of claims from the control plane (service.claims_per_poll), and the heartbeat of its state file and of the running job's lease.

service.queue_stale_s.description: A woken PR not merged after this long warns the queue health check.

service.recent.description: How many merges, wakes and runner results `scripts/service status` lists, newest first.

service.results_kept.description: How many results and done job ids the runner's state file keeps (bounded state).

service.runner_kind_env.description: The variable naming what a runner runs on (box, vm, actions, session, other; contracts/service/result.v1.json).

service.runner_name_env.description: Variables naming a runner in its state and results, the first set one; else the host name.

service.runner_stall_alert_s.description: RUNNER-STALL-ALERT (docs/operations/aws-revisao-arquitetura.md, findings 2 and 3): how long, in seconds, a run the service handed over to the runner (work.run `starting`) may wait to be taken before the live service alerts (platform.runner.stalled, published to the platform's topic once when it starts and once when it ends). A run handed over is taken within a second by a free slot (the service dispatches only up to the runner's registered capacity), and a runner task the rollout replaced warms for 63 s at p50 (80 s at most, scripts/medir prewarm_s); a run not taken is reaped at its lease (5 minutes) and handed over again, so the limit stays under the lease: 180 s covers the warm-up twice and still alerts before the first reap.

service.runner_token_env.description: The variable that holds the runner token of the control plane (its RUNNER_TOKEN secret). Without it a runner refuses to start with an error naming the variable (D-290): there is no other route.

service.self_update.description: GATE-SPEED R6 (D-092): a Tower runner whose checkout's scripts/ changed with the base (a refresh before a train job) re-executes itself between jobs, so a fix merged to the base reaches it without a manual restart. Off is the rollback: it keeps the code it started with until it exits.

service.state_path.description: The Tower runner's state file, relative to its checkout: heartbeat, current job and recent results, written by an atomic rename and read by `scripts/service status|health|metrics`.

default.equals: the control plane's Worker secret RUNNER_TOKEN
default.used_for: claims, heartbeats and results on the control plane

default.equals: the control plane's Worker secret EVENTS_TOKEN
default.used_for: the engine journal (POST and GET /v1/events): the train reads its queue there

default.equals: a fine-grained GitHub token on openuniversity-si/open-university (Contents and Pull requests read/write, Metadata read)
default.used_for: git and the GitHub REST client of the gate and the train

service.token_holders.description: The inventory of every secret a runner needs (D-291 (5), TRAIN-DEFINITIVE R6): per environment variable, what it must equal (the control-plane secret or the account it is a token of), the runner kinds that need it, the file that holds it on the runner and what it is used for. Only names are registered, never a value. A rotation updates every holder listed here, then restarts the runner; a missing variable and a refused token are reported as this entry (scripts/lib/service_credentials.py).

service.transport.description: Where a Tower runner takes its jobs (ADR-41, D-290): the control plane at service.control_url, its only job channel and wake source. `control` is the only value: the git transport was deleted, and a runner reading anything else stops with an error naming this key, never falling back.

service.user_agent.description: The User-Agent every request of a runner to the control plane carries (claim, heartbeat, result), set in one place (ControlTransport.call). The edge in front of today's control plane answers 403 to urllib's default `Python-urllib/<version>`, so a runner without it fell back to git on every poll (GATE-SPEED, D-091). Generic: it names the client, never a vendor.

service.webhook_drop_bad_signature.description: When true a delivery whose signature no key verifies, or that is malformed, is dropped (logged as webhook_dropped); when false it stays in the queue and is retried, e.g. while the forge's rotated key has not arrived. Read per SQS batch from work.config_value (DEP9).

service.webhook_drop_stale.description: When true a delivery outside the freshness window is dropped (deleted from the queue, logged as webhook_dropped); when false it stays in the queue and is retried (then the dead-letter queue). Read per SQS batch from work.config_value (DEP9).

service.webhook_tolerance_s.description: Freshness window of a webhook delivery in the queue consumer: the signed webhook-timestamp may be at most this far from the queue's SentTimestamp. Read per SQS batch from work.config_value (DEP9), the compiled default when no row exists; PUT /v1/config/service.webhook_tolerance_s changes it with no deploy. The port's own accept keeps the compiled 300.
